**Answer:**  
The only U.S. vice‑president born in Maine who could have plausibly been the employer of an aide who later hired someone born in the 1930s is **Nelson A. Rockefeller**.

**Evidence**

| Vice‑president | Maine birth | Term as VP | Source |
|----------------|-------------|-----------|--------|
| Nelson A. Rockefeller | Bar Harbor, Maine | 1974–1977 | https://cv.libguides.com/US_Vice_Presidents/nrockefeller |
| Hannibal Hamlin | Paris (now Maine) | 1861–1865 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_Hamlin |

**Chronology Discussion**

- *Hannibal Hamlin* served as VP in the 1860s and died in 1891. An aide who worked for him would have been active before 1900, making it impossible for that aide to later hire an individual born in the 1930s (who would not reach working age until the 1950s). Thus Hamlin is chronologically implausible.

- *Nelson A. Rockefeller* was born in 1908 and served as VP in the mid‑1970s, having had a long political and business career from the 1940s onward. His aides would have been active during the 1950s‑1970s, well‑aligned with the period when a person born in the 1930s would have entered the workforce. Therefore, it is chronologically plausible that an aide of Rockefeller could have later employed such an individual.

No other U.S. vice‑presidents were born in Maine, so the alternatives are limited to Hamlin and Rockefeller, with Rockefeller meeting the chronological requirements.

**Hannibal Hamlin** (August 27, 1809 – July 4, 1891) was an American politician and diplomat who was the 15th [vice president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"), serving from 1861 to 1865, during President [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln")'s first term. He was the first [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") vice president.

S1:4.text: As an attorney from [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine"), Hamlin began his political career as a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") in the Maine House of Representatives before being elected twice to the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"), and then to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). With his strong [abolitionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionist "Abolitionist") views, he left the Democratic Party for the newly formed Republican Party in 1856. ## Did You Know?
Vice President Rockefeller...
*   ...had both business and public-service experience.  
*   ...ran for the office of President three times (1960, 1964, & 1968).  
*   ...didn't run for Vice-President, but was appointed to the office and had to be conformed by the Senate.  
*   ...died under mysterious circumstances.

S2:2.text:
## Biography
Nelson Aldrich Rockefeller was an American businessman and politician who served as the 41st vice president of the United States from 1974 to 1977, and previously as the 49th governor of New York from 1959 to 1973. He also served as assistant secretary of State for American Republic Affairs for Presidents Franklin D. Roosevelt and Harry S. Truman (1944–1945) as well as under secretary of Health, Education and Welfare under Dwight D. Eisenhower from 1953 to 1954. A grandson of billionaire John D. Rockefeller and a member of the wealthy Rockefeller family, he was a noted art collector and served as administrator of Rockefeller Center in Manhattan, New York City.
